blackout.title: A cold-snap overload blacks out France
blackout.line: On 19 December 1978 an overloaded line near Nancy tripped a cascade that cut power to about three quarters of France.

blackout.title: Turkey’s grid splits in two
blackout.line: On 31 March 2015 a single line failure split Turkey’s strained grid, darkening all 81 provinces and about 76 million people.

blight.title: Coffee rust ruins Ceylon’s plantations
blight.line: Coffee rust reached Ceylon’s single-crop estates around 1869; coffee land shrank from about 111,000 hectares in 1870 to under 5,000 by 1900.

blight.title: Panama disease kills the Gros Michel
blight.line: Panama disease wiped out vast Central American plantings of the Gros Michel banana in the 1950s, forcing exporters to switch to the Cavendish.

blight.title: Southern corn leaf blight strikes
blight.line: A fungus hit hybrids sharing one Texas cytoplasm, found in about 90% of seed sold, cutting the US corn harvest by about 15%.

commune.title: Student-led unrest sweeps France
commune.line: Protests begun by students over failing public services drew 550,000 people across France on 17 October, echoing the 2018 yellow vests.

deepblue.title: A program sweeps the Othello champion
deepblue.line: Michael Buro’s program Logistello beat reigning Othello world champion Takeshi Murakami 6 to 0, three months after Deep Blue’s chess win.

dolly.title: Spallanzani breeds puppies by syringe
dolly.line: Italian priest-scientist Lazzaro Spallanzani artificially inseminated a spaniel, which bore puppies: the first recorded mammal conceived without mating.

dolly.title: A secret donor insemination in Philadelphia
dolly.line: Doctor William Pancoast inseminated a sedated woman with a student’s sperm without telling her; the case stayed secret until 1909.

dust.title: Indonesian haze triggers top regional alert
dust.line: Indonesian fires put Singapore, Malaysia and East Timor on the highest of four haze alerts, turning Borneo skies yellow and orange.

einstein.title: Bomb scientists urge a demonstration first
einstein.line: Seven Manhattan Project scientists, including Szilárd, urged against a surprise atomic attack on Japan and predicted a nuclear arms race.

einstein.title: ELIZA’s creator warns about computers
einstein.line: Joseph Weizenbaum, shaken that people confided in his chatbot ELIZA, argued in a 1976 book that computers must not replace human judgment.

flu.title: The first cholera pandemic
flu.line: Cholera spreads from Bengal across Asia, East Africa and the Mediterranean, the first of seven cholera pandemics.

hamilton.title: Britain absorbs Ireland’s war debts
hamilton.line: When Britain and Ireland merged their exchequers in 1817, one UK fund took on Ireland’s debt, which had nearly quadrupled since 1801.

luddites.title: Vespasian rejects a labour-saving hoist
luddites.line: According to Suetonius, Vespasian paid an engineer for a cheap way to haul columns but refused it, saying he must feed the poor.

luddites.title: Sawyers wreck a wind-powered sawmill
luddites.line: About 500 London sawyers smashed Charles Dingley’s new wind sawmill at Limehouse, saying it robbed them of their work.

mania.title: Melbourne’s land boom collapses
mania.line: Melbourne’s 1880s suburban building boom collapsed from 1891, leaving lenders with thousands of unsaleable houses before banks failed in 1893.

mania.title: Dubai World asks for a debt standstill
mania.line: After building palm-shaped islands and towers on borrowed money, Dubai World sought a standstill on about $59 billion of debt in 2009.

modelt.title: Pascal’s five-sol coaches open in Paris
modelt.line: Blaise Pascal’s shared coaches ran fixed routes at a five-sol fare, opening carriage travel to paying Parisians, until rules barred commoners.

munich.title: Lithuania seizes Klaipėda in staged revolt
munich.line: Lithuanian volunteers in civilian clothes seized Klaipėda in 1923, posing as locals rising to protect persecuted Lithuanians, and the Allies accepted it.

oil.title: Britain chokes off Iran’s oil exports
oil.line: After Iran nationalised its oil, Britain imposed sanctions and its navy intercepted tankers, effectively shutting down Iran’s oil exports.

oil.title: Moscow cuts Lithuania’s oil and gas
oil.line: After Lithuania declared independence, Moscow cut off its oil and gas in April 1990 to force it to back down.

phone.title: Britain’s Uniform Penny Post begins
phone.line: A flat one-penny rate for any letter in Britain made writing cheap, and letter volume more than doubled in the first year.

railway.title: Fare-paying passengers ride the rails
railway.line: On the Swansea and Mumbles line in Wales, horse-drawn carriages began the world’s first regular fare-paying passenger service on rails.

railway.title: The first electric tram carries passengers
railway.line: Siemens & Halske opened a 2.4 km electric tramway at Lichterfelde near Berlin, the first public electric tram in regular service.

scramble.title: Ottomans and Portugal fight for Mombasa
scramble.line: Ottoman corsair Mir Ali Beg won Swahili towns from Portugal, until a Portuguese fleet drove him from Mombasa in 1589.

scramble.title: Oman captures Fort Jesus from Portugal
scramble.line: After a siege of almost three years, Oman seized Portugal’s Fort Jesus, taking over the Swahili coast from a rival foreign power.

suez.title: Dutch ships sail around Africa
suez.line: Shut out of Lisbon’s spice market by war with Spain, which ruled Portugal, the Dutch sent their own ships around Africa.

sykes.title: Belgians revolt against a Vienna-made kingdom
sykes.line: The great powers at Vienna had joined Belgium to the Netherlands as a buffer state; in 1830 Belgian rebels broke away.

sykes.title: Britain partitions Bengal
sykes.line: Curzon’s government split Bengal in 1905; boycotts and revolutionary bombings followed until Britain reversed the partition in 1911.

titanic.title: The luxury liner Arctic sinks
titanic.line: The celebrated, luxurious Collins liner sank after a collision in fog; boats held under half aboard and no woman or child survived.

titanic.title: The R101 airship crashes in France
titanic.line: Britain’s showpiece airship, with a lounge and dining room, left half-tested for India and crashed in France, killing 48 including the Air Minister.

vaccine.title: Japan halts its whooping cough vaccine
vaccine.line: After two infants died following DTP shots, Japan suspended infant pertussis vaccination; coverage fell and cases climbed to a 1979 peak.

volcker.title: Britain jumps Bank Rate to 7%
volcker.line: Chancellor Thorneycroft backed raising Bank Rate from 5% to 7%, arguing inflation had to be squeezed out to save the pound.

volcker.title: Brazil lifts its key rate to 14.25%
volcker.line: With inflation above 9%, Brazil’s central bank raised its Selic rate a sixth straight time, to 14.25%, despite a deepening recession.

y2k.title: A software bug freezes a big bank
y2k.line: New software failed past 32,000 transactions, leaving the bank stuck with bonds it could not deliver and a record $22.6 billion Fed loan.

y2k.title: The Slammer worm jams the internet
y2k.line: A tiny worm spread worldwide in hours, knocking most of Bank of America’s 13,000 ATMs offline and cutting South Korea’s internet.

games.title: Nero wins the Olympic Games
games.line: Emperor Nero had the Games rescheduled and new contests added for his tour of Greece, then was crowned winner despite falling from his chariot.

games.title: Argentina’s junta hosts the World Cup
games.line: The military junta hired a public relations firm to sell “stability” while thousands disappeared, some held less than a mile from the final’s stadium.

games.title: China stages the Beijing Olympics
games.line: China spent an estimated $40 billion on a lavish Olympics, as protests over Tibet followed its torch relay around the world.
